high.title: Bank Deposit Rates as of July 12: ACB Leads Market at 7.3%/Year for 12-Month Term
high.summary: The Vietnamese deposit rate landscape continues to show upward pressure from private and mid-tier banks, with ACB now topping the market at 7.3%/year for 12-month deposits, followed by Saigonbank at 7.2%/year. A total of six banks now offer rates at or above 7.0%/year for 12-month tenors, including MBV, VCBNeo, PGBank, and VIB. The next tier — Bac A Bank, LPBank, BVBank, and OCB — sits at 6.9%/year. Notably, the four state-owned commercial banks (Agribank, BIDV, Vietcombank, VietinBank) have kept their rate schedules unchanged, maintaining a structural divergence with private sector peers.

high.title: Vietcombank Publishes Average Lending Rate Data for May 2026
high.summary:
Vietcombank — Vietnam's largest state-owned commercial bank by market capitalization and a key policy transmission vehicle — has disclosed that its average lending rate for May 2026 reached **7.2% per annum**, marking the **fourth consecutive month of increases**. The spread between average lending and deposit rates stands at 3.5% p.a., while the net interest margin (after funding-related costs) sits at 2.0% p.a.

To contextualise the trajectory: average lending rates were at 6.4% in February 2026, rising to 6.6% in March, and continuing upward through April and May. This represents an **80 basis point increase in three months**, signalling a meaningful tightening in credit pricing across the banking system.

high.title: First Bank to Announce Savings Interest Rate Hike Since Early July
high.summary: Bac A Bank (North Asia Commercial Joint Stock Bank) has become the first Vietnamese bank to raise its listed deposit rates in July 2026, signaling a potential shift in the domestic interest rate environment. The bank raised rates uniformly by 20 basis points (0.2 percentage points) across multiple tenors. Key new rates are as follows: 1–5 month tenors now at 4.75% p.a.; 6–11 month tenors at 7.05% p.a.; the 12-month tenor — the market benchmark — now at 7.10% p.a.; and 13–36 month tenors at 6.95% p.a. Notably, Bac A Bank also simplified its rate structure, eliminating the tiered system that previously differentiated between deposits below and above VND 1 billion, effectively granting all retail depositors access to previously premium rates.

high.title: VN-Index Plunges Nearly 50 Points Before Partial Recovery — What Should Equity Investors Do Next?
high.summary:
Vietnam's equity market opened the new week under severe pressure on July 13, with the VN-Index tumbling as much as 48 points intraday before partial demand absorption trimmed losses to approximately 28 points at the close. The index managed to hold the psychologically critical 1,800-point threshold, but market breadth was decisively negative: 271 stocks declined on HoSE versus only 52 advancers. Within the VN30 large-cap basket, 27 of 30 constituents finished in the red, signaling that selling pressure was concentrated in blue-chips rather than being confined to speculative names. Total matched-order value on HoSE reached approximately VND 17,900 billion — below what would be expected given the magnitude of the intraday swing — indicating that buyers remained cautious and were unwilling to deploy capital aggressively even at lower prices. The partial recovery was reportedly driven by select banking stocks stepping in as support. For fund managers, the key watch points are: (1) whether the 1,800-level holds as durable support on follow-through sessions, (2) foreign net buying/selling flow which will clarify whether this is domestic deleveraging or broader capital outflow, and (3) any SBV signaling on liquidity that could affect bank stock valuations.

---

high.title: Maybank Analysis Director Identifies Key Factor Determining Interest Rate Trends Going Forward
high.summary:
In an interview, Mr. Quan Trong Thanh, Head of Research at Maybank Securities Vietnam, argues that **inflation — not liquidity tightness — is the primary driver of Vietnam's current elevated interest rate environment**. While the system-wide Loan-to-Deposit Ratio (LDR) has risen to approximately 112–115%, with the gap between credit growth and deposit mobilization reaching ~VND 2.6 quadrillion (as of Q1/2026), he cautions against interpreting this in isolation as a signal of abnormal stress.

Critically, he suggests **interest rates could begin to ease as early as September 2026**, conditional on inflation maintaining the favorable trajectory seen in June through July and August. This is a significant forward-looking signal for VND rates traders and bond investors. A September rate softening, if realized, could be a catalyst for duration extension in Vietnamese government bonds. Investors should closely monitor July and August CPI prints as the key trigger. For VND FX, easing rate expectations could narrow the VND carry advantage, worth monitoring against USD dynamics.

---

medium.title: Dragon Capital Names Three Stock Groups with Bright Prospects for H2 2026; One Group Expected to Post 100% Profit Growth
medium.summary:
In its latest strategy report, Dragon Capital outlined three key drivers shaping Vietnam's equity market outlook for H2 2026: (i) accelerated public investment disbursement and supportive monetary/fiscal policies to meet growth targets; (ii) Vietnam's official inclusion in the FTSE Russell Secondary Emerging Market index from September 2026; and (iii) attractive market valuations providing upside potential if corporate earnings growth and liquidity move in tandem. Dragon Capital notes the VN-Index's 2026 forward P/E stands at approximately 11.7x — considered attractive relative to regional peers. Excluding the four Vingroup-related stocks (which account for ~29% of market cap), valuations appear even more compelling. The FTSE upgrade in September is particularly significant for international fund managers, as it is expected to catalyze meaningful passive and active foreign capital inflows into Vietnamese equities, with positive secondary implications for VND demand and domestic liquidity conditions. Investors should monitor foreign net buying trends and any SBV FX intervention activity as the FTSE inclusion date approaches.

---

medium.title: Agribank Publishes Lending Rate Schedule
medium.summary: Agribank has disclosed its average lending rate schedule applicable for May 2026. Priority sector short-term VND loans (in line with government and SBV directives) are priced at 4.0%/year, while standard short-term loans carry a minimum of 6.1%/year and medium-to-long-term loans a minimum of 7.8%/year. Credit card lending is set at 15.0%/year. The bank's average lending rate for the month stood at 8.63%/year against an average cost of funds of 7.16%/year, implying a net interest spread of approximately 147 basis points. As Vietnam's largest bank by assets and a key policy transmission channel, Agribank's lending rate profile provides a useful benchmark for the broader credit environment. The relatively thin spread between cost of funds and lending rates underscores ongoing margin pressure at state-owned banks, a key variable for sector equity investors and those monitoring credit growth dynamics relevant to VND liquidity conditions.

medium.title: Banking Sector Results Update – July 12: Vietcombank Posts Positive H1 2026 Figures; Sacombank Profit Estimated to Halve
medium.summary: Vietcombank reported robust H1 2026 metrics at its mid-year business review conference held on July 10 in Hanoi. Total assets reached nearly VND 2.67 quadrillion (approximately USD 105 billion), up 9.83% from end-2025. Credit outstanding rose 4.8% to VND 1.74 quadrillion, with FDI enterprise lending surging over 16% and SME lending up 10.4%. International payment and trade finance volumes grew 16.1%, reflecting Vietnam's ongoing role as a key node in global supply chain realignment. In contrast, Sacombank's profit is estimated to have fallen by approximately half, a significant underperformance that coincides with the appointment of its first foreign CEO (Loic Faussier). For VN-Index investors, Vietcombank's solid asset growth and FDI-linked lending momentum are positive signals for the banking sector, which carries heavy index weighting. The divergence between Vietcombank and Sacombank also highlights differentiated credit quality and restructuring risks within the sector.

medium.title: Gold Enters a "Pivotal Week" — Experts Highlight Key Factors to Watch Closely
medium.summary:
Global gold prices closed last week at approximately USD 4,120/oz (spot), down 1.32% week-on-week, with COMEX August futures slipping to USD 4,128/oz, bringing year-to-date losses to nearly 6%. The primary driver of weakness was a simultaneous rebound in the US dollar and US Treasury yields, as Fed minutes from the June meeting revealed that several officials remain open to further rate hikes given persistent inflation concerns. Domestically, SJC gold tracked global moves, settling around VND 146.9 million/tael (buy) and VND 149.9 million/tael (sell), down nearly 1% on the week. For VND and rates traders, this dynamic is relevant on two fronts: a stronger USD and higher US yields historically exert depreciation pressure on the VND, and gold price trends in Vietnam can influence retail savings behavior and, by extension, deposit flows into the banking system. Upcoming US economic data releases this week will be the key catalyst to monitor for directional cues on both gold and the USD/VND rate.

---

medium.title: Savings Rates Hit 9% Per Annum — Depositors Restless, Switching Banks at Maturity
medium.summary: Vietnamese retail deposit rates have climbed to as high as **9% per annum**, prompting active switching behavior among savers seeking better yields across competing banks. The spread between institutions is now meaningful — up to 100 basis points between comparable tenors (e.g., 8% vs. 8.8% for similar maturities) — incentivizing deposit migration. MBS Securities' latest research notes that the **upward momentum in deposit rates is showing early signs of plateauing**, which aligns with the Maybank view above. For bond and rates investors, rising deposit rates compress bank NIMs and keep the short end of the yield curve elevated. The retail rate surge also reflects broader system liquidity tightness and could delay any SBV policy pivot. Watch for whether the 9% ceiling holds or pushes higher in coming weeks.

medium.title: Surprising Latest NPL Trends at Vietcombank, Agribank, Sacombank, ABBank...
medium.summary: Mid-year NPL data across major Vietnamese banks presents a **mixed but broadly stable picture**, with one notable outlier. Vietcombank maintains one of the system's lowest NPL ratios at below 1% (Q1/2026: 0.62%). ABBank reported a sharp improvement, with NPL expected to fall to ~0.55% from ~0.85% at end-Q1/2026. Agribank holds steady at a historically low 1.13%. However, **Sacombank is the clear outlier**, with its CEO flagging NPL could surge to **5.6%** (vs. 5.01% at end-Q1/2026), driven by elevated funding costs, legacy ownership-related overhang, NIM compression, and potentially record provisioning charges. For equity investors in Vietnamese bank stocks and for systemic risk assessment relevant to VND and bond markets, Sacombank's deterioration warrants monitoring — elevated provisioning pressures could weigh on sector earnings and credit supply.

medium.title: US and Iran Both Claim Control Over the Strait of Hormuz — Middle East Tensions Escalate
medium.summary:
> ⚠️ **Analyst Note — Indirect Relevance to VND & Vietnamese Markets:**
> Tensions over the Strait of Hormuz escalated after Iran attacked a container vessel on July 12. Both the US and Iran claim authority over the strategic waterway, while UN Secretary-General Guterres warned of "catastrophic consequences" if full-scale conflict resumes. Oil prices surged nearly 5% on July 13 before partially retreating. For Vietnam — a net energy importer — a sustained oil price spike would feed directly into domestic inflation, widen the trade deficit, and add pressure on the VND. The SBV may face a more challenging FX management environment if crude remains elevated. Bond investors should monitor whether imported inflation expectations begin to reprice the short end of the Vietnamese yield curve. This situation warrants close monitoring, though it has not yet produced a direct domestic policy response.
